questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast, where should you ride to have the most room to recover?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most room to control your bike if a wind blast affects you.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle in Colorado?

options.text: All passengers
Passengers under the age of 18
Passengers riding with an operator under age 18
Helmets are not required to be worn by any passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passengers under the age of 18
questions.explanation: In Colorado, all operators and passengers under 18 must wear an approved helmet. All riders should wear a helmet for safety.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means you plan to turn right or change lanes to the right. You can use this hand signal instead of or along with your turn signals.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Try to get onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This is safest and discourages the other driver from returning to your lane too soon.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you come to a full stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.
questions.explanation: Release the brake lever when your front wheel locks. Once the tire regains traction, you can apply the brake again.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you ride?

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind. This tells the other driver not to return to your lane until it is safe.

questions.question: During the day, how should you use your headlight?

options.text: Not be used.
Be used on its high beam setting.
Be used on its low beam setting.
Alternate between high beam and low beam settings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used on its high beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day. This helps other drivers see you. Use high beam any time you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before contact.
Slow down before contact.
Lean the motorcycle.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible before hitting the object. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front end just before impact.

questions.question: If your throttle becomes stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Try twisting the throttle back and forth several times to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When approaching a police officer.
When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is following you too closely. This alerts the other driver. It also helps warn drivers if you are slowing down in a place where they might not expect it.

questions.question: When preparing to pass on the left, why should you ride on the left side of your lane?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It gives you a better view of hazards in the next lane.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It places you in the rearview mirror of the car in front.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a better view of hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of your lane increases your ability to see ahead. It also makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip for better traction.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Don't worry about oil or other items in a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of each lane. On dry roads, this strip usually has enough grip for motorcycles. When the road is wet, avoid it. The strip is usually narrow enough that you can ride around it and stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly creep up.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. The vehicle could back up suddenly, or you may need space to escape from traffic coming from behind.

questions.question: On a wet road, which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.
All areas of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of the lane. On dry roads, this strip has enough grip for motorcycles. On wet roads, avoid it. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it and stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Don't swerve and only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first, then swerve, or swerve first, then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: ______ guarantees that another driver sees you.

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that another driver sees you. Assume that any vehicle that can enter your path will. Stay alert and defensive.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycle brakes?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal stopping power.
The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more stopping power than the front brake.
Only use the front brake when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of the total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left position
The center position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change. Pick a position that gives you the most space and makes other drivers see you better.

questions.question: What is the right footwear for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Has long, loose laces.
Has short heels.
Has tall heels.
Is always sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on surfaces. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught.

questions.question: Who should set the speed for a group of riders?

options.text: The leader
The riders just behind the leader
The rider in back
The oldest rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider in back
questions.explanation: The last rider in the group should set the pace. This makes sure no riders get left behind.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than you would normally.
Start slowing earlier than you would normally.
Increase your following distance.
Not communicate with the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not communicate with the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower, slow down sooner, and keep more distance from other vehicles. Always tell your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Not use your headlight.
Alternate between your headlight's low and high beam settings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If your rear tire locks on a surface with good grip, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a good surface, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.
